input: Join /data/employees.csv and /data/departments.csv on the department_id field. Produce /data/report.csv with columns: name, department_name, salary. Include a header row. Print the result.

transcript.final_response:
I joined the two files on `department_id` and saved the result as `/data/report.csv`:

```
name,department_name,salary
Alice,Engineering,120000
Bob,Marketing,95000
Carol,Engineering,115000
Dave,Sales,88000
Eve,Marketing,92000
```

Every employee's `department_id` matched a department, so all 5 employees are in the report, in their original order. If an ID had no match, that employee would still appear but with an empty department name.

I used a short `awk` script that splits on commas. That works for this data, but it would break if any field contained a quoted comma.
tool_calls: cd /data; ls; head -n 50 employees.csv departments.csv; wc -l employees.csv departments.csv

cd /data; awk -F, 'NR==FNR{if(FNR>1)d[$1]=$2;next} FNR==1{print "name,department_name,salary";next} {sub(/\r$/,"");print $1","(($2 in d)?d[$2]:"")","$3}' departments.csv employees.csv > report.csv; cat report.csv
